item.title: Nishiawakura: The Japanese village reborn through its forest
item.description: Faced with a shrinking and aging population, the village crafted this strategy in collaboration with forestry experts and rural development planners. The goal? To revitalize the local economy by sustainably managing the forest that covers 95% of its land.

item.title: Building with purpose: Honest conversations on sustainability in architecture & design
item.description: Emerging designers are entering the field at a critical moment. The advice shared by experienced professionals is clear: learn the fundamentals of sustainability, stay curious, and don’t be afraid to question traditional practices. It’s important to remember that sustainability is not about achieving perfection. It’s about honesty, transparency, and a willingness to evolve. Companies and brands must be allowed space to experiment, to fail, and to learn.

item.title: Green dreams in Turin: The progressive architecture behind Green Pea’s sustainability-focused shopping experience
item.description: Green Pea is an ambitious project. Its architecture, materials, and storytelling make it a symbol of urban change, aligned with the environmental challenges of our time. Even if its large-scale impact is still developing and its message mainly reaches a specific audience, Green Pea fulfills a vital role as a demonstrative space. It inspires, educates, and raises new questions about the role of sustainability in our everyday lives. By merging commerce with consciousness, it invites us to rethink.

item.title: The Greener Space: Practical Design Tips
item.description: As the world faces environmental challenges, architects, designers, and policymakers are increasingly turning to greener living strategies to create spaces that benefit both people and the planet. But what does embracing greener living really mean? How can it be applied effectively in architecture and design? This article explores practical strategies that make greener living achievable and impactful.

item.title: Green Artillery: How could railroads turn into humanistic green corridors?
item.description: Railroads are essential and indispensable modes of transportation in modern cities. These superstructures physically, socially, and economically connect various neighborhoods. However, these massive structures do not typically include appealing places where people want to spend their time in daily life. Recently, this trend has begun to change, driven by initiatives aimed at addressing the challenges posed by the physical barriers created by railroads.

item.title: Nature meets future in Pujiang
item.description: An ambitious urban development is taking shape in Pujiang, a town south of Chengdu, China, with the goal of delivering a sustainable, high-quality lifestyle. Already known for its clean air and green hills, the project aims to preserve this natural setting while minimizing environmental impact and addressing future risks. A simple tourist platform overlooks the town and the surrounding Qionglai mountain range. Studio MVRDV was invited to reimagine the Pujiang platform.

item.title: From Hospital to Green District: Cidade Matarazzo, São Paulo
item.description: Cidade Matarazzo introduces a different kind of urban experience. Starting from an existing hospital building that was carefully preserved, the site has been transformed into a modern district designed to bring life, greenery, and cultural activity to a historic corner of São Paulo.
